insight: When evaluating art directions that depend on lighting/animation/VFX (e.g. trail glow, dither textures, emissive materials, particle bursts), build 4-5 live Three.js mockup scenes in a companion page rather than static AI-gen images. Reasons: (1) Director sees the actual character mesh in each lighting model, not an artistic interpretation. (2) VFX behavior can't be judged from still frames. (3) Side-by-side with same scene composition makes the differences pop. (4) Browser WebGL context limit is ~16 so up to ~10 panels works without render-to-image dance. (5) Cost ~comparable to AI-gen iteration + curation. Used in 2026-04-30 visual direction plan when ComfyUI was unreachable from WSL.

When 4 visual directions feel too similar, the cheapest fix is per-direction FX vocabulary, not changing palettes. Same gameplay event (claim/kill/respawn/win) reads differently in each direction when each owns its own particle style, motion, and timing. Background swap alone is not enough — directions must differ at moments of action.

When adding a visual direction whose ground is NOT at Y=0 (e.g., island raised on a sand cylinder), every positionally-anchored element needs to lift: territory mesh Y, character group.position.y, trail mesh Y, respawn-build start/end Y, particle ground-ring Y, claim-FX entry Y. Pattern: store this._islandTopY on the scene, read it everywhere with || 0 fallback, all existing direction logic still works.

Mockup uses ARENA_RADIUS=10 but game uses ARENA_RADIUS=66.89. Geometry written as ARENA_RADIUS*N scales fine; absolute-unit dimensions (cliff-rocks 0.5-1.0u, atoll widths, sand cylinder height) need rescaling at game scale or they'll look like pebbles. Always check the host's constants.js before porting mockup geometry.

When porting a mockup that introduces a raised ground (sand cylinder + grass top), define a single _islandTopY constant on the Game and route ALL surface-bound geometry through it: territory mesh, character group base Y, trail mesh Y, camera lookAt Y, respawn-build Y. Missing any one drops things below the water plane invisibly. Pass baseY into Character constructor (not via global) so the renderer Character class can also re-assert it in syncVisuals.

Procedural shaders ported from a mockup with a smaller ARENA_RADIUS will have wavelengths that look like noise at game scale. Divide spatial frequencies (sin coefficients) by the radius ratio so wavelengths map proportionally. For our case mockup ARENA_RADIUS=10 vs game=66.89 → divide by ~6 (e.g. p.x*0.35 → p.x*0.06). Same applies to foam ring widths and any 'absolute' size measured in world units.

When stacking a flat 3D mesh (CylinderGeometry top face) with a textured plane (territory mesh), separating them by >=0.05 units AND making the top mesh face the only surface at that Y level eliminates Z-fighting at all camera angles — far more reliable than relying on transparent-mesh render order. Pattern: declare named Y reference fields (_islandTopY, _fxRingY) and let every layered surface compute its own Y as offset-from-reference. Director quote: 'the floor of the island is not the same height as the base of the battlefield so not to have them intersecting.'

When a Director gives a SPATIAL constraint about UI ('notifications must appear BELOW the leaderboard, not on top of any other UI element'), don't just code the position — render dashed-outline placeholder rectangles for ALL the constrained-against UI elements (factions, leaderboard, minimap, player stats) so the screenshot itself proves the constraint is satisfied. Without ghosts, the Director can't verify; with ghosts, the screenshot is self-documenting. The ghosts cost ~80 lines of CSS-in-JS and gate a single config flag (showLeaderboardGhost: true) so they're trivial to opt-out for non-spatial-constrained directions.
